judgements.justification: No criticism rested on a wrong factual claim; every checkable criticism in either committee (3GRx's pointer, AuTG's typos, px8j's Theorem 2.1) was correct.
B's spotlight sits on 7, 6, 8, 8 with two reasoned or confident 8s; the chair's 'foundational advance' adds wording, not a tier above the scores.
B's Reviewer_91N9 gave an 8 on three sentences of praise with no weakness, lifting B's mean; A's UuHj gave a 7 without verifying the arguments.
Both forums got the same concessions: Proposition 2.2 is replaceable and other applications are only asserted.
No substantive flaw was found; the flagged defects are typos and presentation slips that neither committee needed to weigh.
The rebuttal lifted B's Reviewer_px8j to 6, while no score in A moved.
The one-sided concerns are presentation details (notation in A, integer coordinates and homogeneity in B) that drove neither tier; the audience concern is not checkable and is covered by R33.
Both committees saw Theorem 1.4 as a synthesis whose new step is Proposition 2.3; A's AuTG gave 6 for it and B's 48Ey gave 8.
B's meta-review tracks Reviewer_48Ey point by point and gives no other argument for a spotlight; its own technical account is wrong about the source of the sample dependence.
AuTG agreed the result is 'somewhat niche' after reading the others but kept the score; no score moved for that reason.
The reply to 3GRx skipped the writing points, but 3GRx's 6 rested on venue fit, so the omission held nothing down.
A's rK8U gave an unargued 6 and never replied; B's 91N9 gave an unargued 8 and added only 'no questions'; both counted unchallenged.
Neither chair went below its reviewers; A's poster matches its 6.25 mean.
A's chair chose a poster for a stated reason (a 'handful of experts' audience), not a mean threshold.
No reviewer in either committee held a below-threshold score.
Both committees read the paper as the same kind of theory contribution to learning Massart halfspaces.
px8j raised on the rebuttal, but did not say the core was outside expertise; the raise addressed presentation questions.
Neither committee demanded a deliverable of this paper type that the other waived; the split concerns audience breadth, covered by R33.
A's UuHj based the 7 on knowing no other use of Forster transforms, though the paper builds on several; B's 91N9 called it 'the first polynomial-time algorithm', which [DGT19] already was.
AuTG kept 6 after the novelty answer and cited niche appeal, but 6 is above threshold.
No committee refused or relied on promised revisions; both judged the same paper.
No reviewer stated a stance that differed from the score.
No extra reviewer was called in.
Clarity verdicts split within B (px8j unclear, 48Ey clear), not between committees, and did not set either tier.
px8j's raise came with a stated reason in a post-rebuttal edit.
Neither chair set aside a silent reviewer; A's silent rK8U and 3GRx counted.
B's Reviewer_48Ey gave a reasoned 8 at confidence 4 and the chair adopted its case; A's highest rating was UuHj's unverified 7.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading with high confidence.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review states a case for the higher tier ('a foundational advance', an elegant idea, new applications), thin as it is.
Both committees had reviewers who knew the [HKLM20], [HM13] and [AKS20] literature (AuTG in A; 48Ey and Nd9v in B).
Neither meta-review misstates reviewers' final positions; B's error concerns the paper's technical content, not the reviewers.

added.name: Narrow-audience objection capped one committee's tier
added.definition: Reviewers or the area chair in one committee judged the paper sound but of interest to few readers or better suited to another venue, and held it to a lower tier on that ground, while the other committee raised no concern about breadth.
added.justification: The main cause is a significance objection about audience and venue raised only in A; R07 needs a checkable concern, R08 needs both committees to have seen the weakness, and R18 needs a demanded deliverable, so none fits.

reasoning: Both committees agreed on the facts: a sound synthesis whose new step is Proposition 2.3. The tier gap comes mainly from A's reviewers and chair judging the payoff too narrow for a broad NeurIPS audience, which no B reviewer raised; no existing reason names that, so R33 is added. The same synthesis was weighted differently (R08), B had a reasoned champion whom its chair followed (R27, R09), the rebuttal moved only B's px8j (R06), and both committees counted thin or unverified high-ish scores (R03, R12, R19).
